x-m-e3-01.title: Different Ways to Share 72 Candies Equally Between Plates
x-m-e3-01.goal: Find several ways wey meet the conditions together (the range for number of plates and candies on each plate), and explain how number of plates and candies on one plate pair together.
x-m-e3-01.material: You wan put 72 candies on plates and share dem equally with nothing left. The number of candies on each plate change depending on how many plates you use.

x-m-e3-01.prereq.0: You fit read multiplication table (you fit use am while you solve)

x-m-e3-01.s.s1.prompt: From the choices for number of plates, choose all the numbers of plates wey let you share 72 candies equally with nothing left.
x-m-e3-01.s.s1.hint.0: For each number of plates, divide 72 by that number and check whether remainder dey.
x-m-e3-01.s.s1.hint.1: Write inside table the numbers of plates wey leave remainder and the ones wey no leave any.
x-m-e3-01.s.s1.r.a: This option come from dividing 72 by 4 and checking say no remainder dey.

x-m-e3-01.s.s1.r.c: This option come from dividing 72 by 6 and checking say no remainder dey.
x-m-e3-01.s.s1.r.d: Multiples of 7 skip past am: 70, 77. If you guess say e go work because the number even, check the products yourself.
x-m-e3-01.s.s1.r.e: This option come from dividing 72 by 9 and checking say no remainder dey.
x-m-e3-01.s.s1.explain: You fit share the candies equally with nothing left only when number of plates times number of candies on one plate equal 72. 4×18, 6×12, and 9×8 na 72, and no number wey you multiply by 5 or 7 go make 72.
x-m-e3-01.s.s2.prompt: You go use at least 2 and at most 9 plates, and you wan put more than 10 candies for each plate. Make 3 ways with different number of plates so you fit share 72 candies equally with nothing left.
x-m-e3-01.s.s2.hint.0: First choose the number of plates, then divide 72 by am to find number of candies for each plate.
x-m-e3-01.s.s2.hint.1: Check one by one say the pair you find follow both conditions (number of plates between range, and more than 10 candies for each plate).
x-m-e3-01.s.s2.var.b: Number of candies on one plate

x-m-e3-01.s.s2.ok.c2: Number of plates na at least 2 and at most 9.
x-m-e3-01.s.s2.fail.c2: Number of plates no dey between 2 and 9.
x-m-e3-01.s.s2.ok.c3: You put more than 10 candies on each plate.
x-m-e3-01.s.s2.fail.c3: You need put more than 10 candies on each plate.
x-m-e3-01.s.s2.ok.c4: Number of plates × number of candies na 72.
x-m-e3-01.s.s2.fail.c4: Number of plates × number of candies no be 72. Multiply again.
x-m-e3-01.s.s2.explain: 2×36, 3×24, 4×18, and 6×12 all equal 72. With 8 or 9 plates, each plate go get less than 10 candies, so e no meet the conditions.
x-m-e3-01.s.s2.because.prompt: Put the ways you make side by side. As number of plates increase, wetin happen to number of candies for each plate? Write your answer with the numbers you make.
x-m-e3-01.s.s2.because.hint.0: Write your ways in order, start from the smallest number of plates.
x-m-e3-01.s.s2.because.hint.1: Compare one after the other how number of plates change and how number of candies change.
x-m-e3-01.s.s2.because.placeholder: Example: When the plates increase from 2 to 3, ...

x-m-e3-01.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: You connect am to the fact say number of plates times candies na always 72?
x-m-e3-01.s.s2.because.model.0: As number of plates go 2, 3, 4, number of candies on one plate go down: 36, 24, 18. When you multiply the two numbers, e always give 72.
x-m-e3-01.s.s2.because.model.1: If you use more plates, each plate get fewer candies. With 3 plates na 24 candies each, and with 6 plates na 12.

x-m-e3-02.s.s3.hint.0: Find how many remain if you give each of the 4 people 1 more out of the 5 remaining candies.

x-m-e3-02.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You explain with your own words why remainder must small pass divisor?
x-m-e3-02.s.s3.model.0: 85÷4=21 ··· 1. 5 remain, but you fit give 1 more to each of the 4 people, so you fit share again. Remainder must small pass divisor 4.
x-m-e3-02.s.s3.model.1: If you give each person 21 candies, 4×21=84 and 1 remain. Remainder 5 bigger than 4, so you fit share again, which mean Seoyeon answer wrong.
x-m-e3-02.s.s3.model.2: Quotient na 21 and remainder na 1. 5 no fit remain. Na because if e pass 4, you fit divide again.
x-m-e3-02.s.s3.model.3: 85÷4=21 remainder 1. Remainder no suppose bigger than divisor, and 5 bigger than 4, so e wrong.

x-m-e3-03.s.s1.r.d: How many numbers dem write no concern length. How many spaces e cover on tape measure na the reason.

x-m-e3-03.s.s2.prompt: This time we get string wey long 0.3 m and another wey long 4/10 m (four tenths of one meter). Which one longer? Use tape measure marks write your reason.
